name: tet Sco

distance_ly.source: Lewis et al. 2022, MNRAS 513, 1129; revised Hipparcos parallax 9.90 +/- 0.26 mas (101 pc)

notes: Lewis et al. conclude the star is undermassive for its luminosity and rotating too fast for its evolutionary stage, most probably a binary merger product. Their reanalysis of the Hipparcos data (binary solution) replaces the catalogue parallax, moving the star from 300 to 329 ly. McDonald et al. 2017 give 6,404 K, 1,118 Lsun, 27.2 Rsun at the old distance.

name: bet CMa

luminosity_lsun.source: Shull, Curran & Topping 2025, arXiv:2508.03800 (log L = 4.41 +/- 0.06, at 151 pc)

radius_rsun.source: Abe et al. (MAGIC Collaboration) 2026, arXiv:2611.04650; asteroseismic model, +/-0.5

notes: Radius is contested: Shull et al. 2025 derive 8.44+/-0.56 Rsun and 13+/-1 Msun from the angular diameter at the Hipparcos distance (151+/-5 pc), while the asteroseismic 10.5+/-0.5 Rsun is in 2.5-sigma tension with that and, per Wikipedia, corresponds to 179+/-10 pc (580 ly); that distance was not confirmed in the paper and is left out. GCVS gives a range of 1.87 to 1.90 in the Hipparcos band. It sits in the Local Bubble's low-density tunnel, so the map-based A_V of 0.34 is probably far too high.
